Compact connected fibers establish section descent; matched volume gives the exact smooth-norm isometry and kernel identity. Matched-volume existence, transformed norms, transferred measures, intrinsic exponent n, and compact realizations are established. The extraction, independent proof, and summaries retain the restrictions on metrics, norms, fibers, and singular selectors.
reconstruction.statement:
Fibration transfer with an isolated non-descending singular selector, with supporting dependency w7-1/n2.

Let (Y,x,L,h,ν_Y), q_m, V_m, B_m, r_j, ε_j, d_j, H_j, G_j, g_j, a, and ω be as in w7-1/n2. In particular, Y=(CP¹)^n, n≥2, the integers r_j≥2 include at least two unequal values, ε_j>0, d_j=r_j+1, and q_m→∞ with q_m=o(m). Put D=∏_jd_j.

Let π:X→Y be a holomorphic submersion of compact complex manifolds with connected fibers of positive complex dimension f. Set N=n+f=dim_C X. Give X any Hermitian manifold structure, and let E=π*L with h_E=π*h. Choose a smooth positive volume ν_X satisfying
π_*ν_X=ν_Y.
Fix p∈π^(−1)(x). In holomorphic submersion coordinates (z,w) centered at p, where z∈C^n, w∈C^f and π(z,w)=z, choose χ_p equal near p to
log(Σ_{j=1}^n|z_j|²+Σ_{ℓ=1}^f|w_ℓ|²),
smooth on X\{p}, and smoothly cut off to zero outside a larger coordinate neighborhood. Such χ_p is quasi-plurisubharmonic. Define
Ψ_m=(q_m+N−1)χ_p,
I_m=I(Ψ_m),
where I(Ψ_m) consists of holomorphic germs F locally integrable with density |F|²exp(−Ψ_m) against any smooth positive volume. The convention is exp(−Ψ_m), not exp(−2Ψ_m).

The selector and selected space satisfy
I_m=𝔪_p^(q_m),
W_m:=H⁰(X,E^m⊗I_m)=π*H⁰(Y,L^m⊗𝔪_x^(q_m))=π*V_m.
Here 𝔪_p is the maximal holomorphic ideal of p. More precisely, a holomorphic germ at p is in I_m exactly when its vanishing order is at least q_m; away from p, I_m is the unit ideal. Thus I_m is coherent. Neither Ψ_m nor I_m descends from Y: Ψ_m is singular at p but finite at other points of π^(−1)(x), and I_m is proper at p but is the unit ideal at those other points. In particular I_m is not the pullback of an ideal sheaf on Y.

For every m≥1, independently of the selector, pullback is a bijection
H⁰(Y,L^m)→H⁰(X,π*L^m).
For a pullback section its order at p equals the order of the base section at x. Give W_m the smooth Hilbert norm
∥S∥_X²=∫_X|S|_{h_E^m}²dν_X.
The singular selector Ψ_m is not included in this norm. For every s∈V_m,
∥π*s∥_X=∥s∥_Y.
If B_X,m is the diagonal partial Bergman kernel of W_m in this norm, then the exact pointwise equality
B_X,m=B_m∘π
holds on X.

Local transfer. Fix τ∈ℝ. For every sequence P_m∈X whose projections z_m=π(P_m) lie in the indicated affine neighborhood, put t_{j,m}=|z_{j,m}|² and μ_{j,m}=mH_j(t_{j,m}). Suppose
 t_{j,m}→0,
 μ_{j,m}/q_m→α_j>0,   Σ_jα_j=1,
 (Σ_jμ_{j,m}−q_m)/√(Σ_jmG_j(t_{j,m}))→τ.
Then
π^n a(t_m)B_X,m(P_m)/[m^n∏_jg_j(t_{j,m})]→Φ(τ).
There is no condition on the positions P_m inside their fibers or on the phases of their projected coordinates. All corrected-center observation scales and all homogeneous-center conclusions of w7-1/n2 transfer without alteration. In particular, for fixed α_j>0 summing to one, R=Σ_jα_jr_j and T_m=q_m+τ√(Rq_m), the corrected radii t_{j,m}=H_j^(-1)(α_jT_m/m) give this law for every q_m=o(m). For homogeneous radii t_{j,m}=(α_jT_m/(r_jm))^(1/r_j), put r_*=max_jr_j and
C_α=(1/√R)Σ_{j:r_j=r_*}(r_*+1)ε_j(α_j/r_*)^(1+1/r_*).
Then
π^nB_X,m(P_m)/[m^n∏_jr_j²|z_{j,m}|^(2r_j−2)]
converges to Φ(τ) if q_m=o(m^(2/(r_*+2))), to Φ(τ+C_αc^((r_*+2)/(2r_*))) if q_m/m^(2/(r_*+2))→c∈(0,∞), and to 1 if that ratio tends to infinity while q_m=o(m). The small-remainder condition is necessary and sufficient for the unshifted homogeneous-center law for every fixed τ along the whole sequence.

Intrinsic section growth and global measure transfer. For all sufficiently large m,
dim W_m=∏_j(d_jm+1)−binomial(q_m+n−1,n),
dim W_m/m^n→D,
lim_{m→∞} log(dim W_m)/log m=n.
The intrinsic exponent is n, not N. Define the smooth nonnegative density
ρ=(ω^n/n!)/ν_Y.
Then
m^(−n)B_X,mν_X ⇒ (ρ∘π)ν_X
weakly on X. The limit has total mass D. Dividing by dim W_m instead gives the probability-measure limit
(dim W_m)^(−1)B_X,mν_X ⇒ (ρ∘π)ν_X/D.
Since f>0, normalization by m^N instead gives the zero measure.
For every continuous A on X, there is a continuous function T_A on Y defined by
π_*(Aν_X)=T_Aν_Y,
with |T_A|≤∥A∥_∞ and T_1=1. The exact integral identity is
∫_X A B_X,m dν_X=∫_Y T_A B_m dν_Y.

Matched volumes and transformed norms. For every such compact holomorphic submersion, matched smooth positive volumes exist. Given any smooth positive volume μ_X, its pushforward has the form
π_*μ_X=bν_Y
with b a smooth positive function. The volume
ν_X=μ_X/(b∘π)
satisfies π_*ν_X=ν_Y and can be realized as the volume of a Hermitian metric on X.
For any arbitrary smooth positive volume ν′_X, without the matched condition, the exact transformed base norm is
∥π*s∥_(ν′_X)²=∫_Y|s|_{h^m}²d(π_*ν′_X).
If π_*ν′_X=bν_Y, this is ∫_Y|s|_{h^m}²b dν_Y. Thus the transformed base volume is bν_Y, not ν_Y. The numerical local limits above are asserted under the matched condition; this norm identity alone does not assert those limits for an arbitrary b.

Compact realizations. Let F be any connected compact Hermitian manifold of dimension f≥1, and let ν_F be a smooth positive volume of mass one. Then X=Y×F, π the projection, E=π*L, and ν_X=ν_Yν_F satisfy the hypotheses. More generally,
ν_X=W(y,u)ν_Yν_F
is matched whenever W>0 is smooth and ∫_F W(y,u)dν_F(u)=1 for every y. Such nonproduct volumes include W=1+δb₀(y)c(u), where b₀ and c are smooth real-valued functions, ∫_F c dν_F=0, and δ is small enough to ensure positivity. The selector at p=(x,p_F) remains isolated and non-descending in these realizations. The volume construction and transfer statements do not require X to be a product.

Scope. The transfer requires connected compact fibers, a pullback line bundle and metric, the specified selector, and a matched or explicitly transformed smooth Hilbert volume. No general transfer is asserted for arbitrary fiber-selected singularities, whose intersection with pullback sections can impose a different base ideal or section space, nor for disconnected fibers, non-pullback bundles or metrics, singular Hilbert norms, or mixed anisotropic base remainders. The theorem does not solve the unrestricted higher-dimensional programme or the original arbitrary-weight one-dimensional problem.
reconstruction.proof:
We use the compact base theorem w7-1/n2 and its exact section and kernel statements. The additional ingredients—section descent, the selector, and integration along fibers—are proved below.

1. Volumes and fiber integration. A nonempty compact holomorphic submersion to the connected Y is onto: its image is open by the submersion coordinates and closed by compactness. Its fibers are smooth compact complex manifolds of dimension f.

For any smooth positive volume μ_X, integration along the fibers gives π_*μ_X=bν_Y with b smooth and positive. Here is a local verification, avoiding any requirement of a global product decomposition. In submersion coordinates (y,w), a volume has a smooth positive density times Euclidean base and fiber volumes. Insert a smooth partition of unity subordinate to finitely many such coordinate charts, with the partition functions supported compactly inside their charts. Near a fixed base point, extend each supported chart density by zero and integrate in w. Differentiation under the integral gives a smooth base density. The sum is the pushforward density. Positivity follows since every fiber is nonempty and the original density is strictly positive. The identical construction for a continuous function A on X proves continuity of the density of π_*(Aμ_X), using uniform continuity on the compact chart supports and dominated convergence.

Multiplication by a base function commutes with pushforward. Thus ν_X=μ_X/(b∘π) satisfies π_*ν_X=ν_Y. It is smooth and positive. Every smooth positive volume on X is the volume of a Hermitian metric: start with a Hermitian metric with volume v, write the desired volume as cv with c>0 smooth, and multiply its Hermitian form by c^(1/N). The volume, the N-th exterior power divided by N!, is multiplied by c. This proves existence and Hermitian realizability of matched volumes.

Under the matched condition define T_A by π_*(Aν_X)=T_Aν_Y. The preceding local construction proves continuity for continuous A; positivity of integration gives |T_A|≤∥A∥_∞ and T_1=1. These assertions apply also to complex-valued A by taking the absolute value bound inside the fiber integral.

2. An isolated non-descending selector. In a submersion coordinate ball centered at p write v=(z,w)∈C^N. Choose a smooth cutoff equal to one on a smaller ball and supported compactly in the coordinate ball, and multiply log|v|^2 by it, defining the result to be zero outside the chart and −∞ at p. This is the required χ_p. It is smooth away from p. Near p it is plurisubharmonic, since log|v|^2 has nonnegative complex Hessian away from zero and its usual plurisubharmonic extension at zero. On the cutoff annulus its complex Hessian is bounded below, and outside it the function is smooth. Compactness then provides a bound dd^cχ_p≥−Cγ for a fixed Hermitian form γ. Equivalently, in each coordinate neighborhood it becomes plurisubharmonic after adding a sufficiently large smooth quadratic function. Thus it is quasi-plurisubharmonic. Multiplication by the positive coefficient q_m+N−1 preserves this property.

We compute its integrability ideal directly with the convention exp(−Ψ_m). Smooth positive volumes are comparable with Euclidean volume on a small ball. If a nonzero holomorphic germ F has order ℓ, write its Taylor series as a sum of homogeneous polynomials beginning with a nonzero polynomial of degree ℓ. Their restrictions to spheres are orthogonal between different degrees: invariance of spherical measure under multiplication by e^{iθ} makes their cross integrals zero. Hence the spherical average of |F(Rθ)|^2 is bounded below by cR^(2ℓ) for small R; it is also bounded above by CR^(2ℓ). Near p the singular density is R^(−2(q_m+N−1)), so the relevant radial integrability criterion is
∫_0^δ R^(2ℓ+2N−1−2(q_m+N−1))dR
=∫_0^δ R^(2(ℓ−q_m)+1)dR<∞.
This holds exactly when ℓ≥q_m; for ℓ=q_m−1 the integral already diverges logarithmically. The zero germ poses no exception. Away from p the weight is smooth and bounded on small neighborhoods, so its ideal is the unit ideal there. Consequently
I(Ψ_m)=m_p^(q_m).
Its coherence follows from the finite monomial resolution in local coordinates, as in the elementary ideal argument of w7-1/n2, now with N variables.

Because f>0, the fiber over x contains a point other than p. The function Ψ_m is singular at p and finite at that other point, so it cannot be the pullback of a function on Y. Likewise its ideal is proper at p and the unit ideal at all other points of that fiber. The extension of a proper base ideal at x is proper at every point over x: in submersion coordinates its generators depend on z alone and have zero value at z=0. If the base ideal is the unit ideal at x, its extension is the unit ideal at all those points. Therefore I_m cannot be the pullback of any base ideal. This proves the specified non-descending nature of both the selector and its ideal.

3. Descent of all holomorphic sections. Pullback is injective because π is onto. To prove surjectivity, trivialize L^m on a base open set U. A section S of π*L^m over π^(−1)U then has a holomorphic scalar coefficient F. On each fiber, this coefficient is a holomorphic function on a connected compact complex manifold, hence constant. The last fact follows from the maximum-modulus principle: at a point attaining its modulus maximum the function is locally constant, and the maximum set propagates over the connected manifold.

Thus F is constant on each fiber. The resulting scalar function on U is holomorphic, since the holomorphic submersion theorem supplies a local holomorphic section of π near each base point and composing F with that section is holomorphic. The resulting functions agree on overlaps and transform by the base bundle transition functions. They define s∈H^0(Y,L^m) with S=π*s. This establishes the asserted bijection for every m, independently of the selector.

In submersion coordinates the coefficient of π*s is s(z), independent of w. Its first nonzero total Taylor degree in (z,w) is therefore exactly its first nonzero degree in z. Vanishing order is invariant under changes of coordinates and nonvanishing frames. Hence ord_p(π*s)=ord_x(s), including the zero section. Combining this with the selector computation gives the exact equality
W_m=H^0(X,E^m⊗I_m)=π*H^0(Y,L^m⊗m_x^(q_m))=π*V_m.
Although the ideal does not descend as a sheaf, its action on the globally fiber-constant section space is exactly this base point-jet condition.

4. Exact Hilbert norm and kernel transfer. Pointwise, |π*s|_(h_E^m)^2=|s|_(h^m)^2∘π. With the matched volume,
∥π*s∥_X^2=∫_X(|s|_(h^m)^2∘π)dν_X=∫_Y|s|_(h^m)^2dν_Y=∥s∥_Y^2.
These are smooth Hilbert norms; no singular selector factor is inserted. A base orthonormal basis therefore pulls back to an orthonormal basis of W_m. Summing its pointwise norms proves for all m the exact identity
B_X,m=B_m∘π,
including the case of a zero section space.

For an arbitrary smooth positive ν′_X the same calculation instead gives
∥π*s∥_(ν′_X)^2=∫_Y|s|_(h^m)^2d(π_*ν′_X).
The pushforward computation in step 1 writes π_*ν′_X=bν_Y with b smooth and positive. Thus the transformed base Hilbert volume is exactly bν_Y. This proves the requested norm transformation, without asserting that the matched-volume numerical kernel asymptotics persist for every b.

5. Local limits, all scales, and section growth. The observations in the note project to observations satisfying exactly the local hypotheses of w7-1/n2: every t_{j,m} tends to zero, every μ_{j,m}/q_m tends to the stipulated positive α_j, and the sum of their true centers has the stated standardized displacement. Applying that theorem and the pointwise equality in step 4 gives
π^n a(t_m)B_X,m(P_m)/[m^n∏_jg_j(t_{j,m})]→Φ(τ).
No property of P_m within its fiber is needed because the kernel is fiber-constant. Phases are unrestricted for the same reason they were unrestricted in the radial base theorem.

For the corrected observations H_j^(−1)(α_jT_m/m), w7-1/n2 verifies all these hypotheses for every q_m→∞ with q_m=o(m); they therefore transfer verbatim. For the homogeneous observations (α_jT_m/(r_jm))^(1/r_j), the same theorem supplies the three regimes with threshold m^(2/(r_*+2)), critical constant C_α, and limiting values Φ(τ), Φ(τ+C_αc^((r_*+2)/(2r_*))), and 1. The prefactors on X are unchanged because of the exact kernel equality. Its necessity-and-sufficiency argument also transfers: projection realizes those radii, π is onto, and every lift has the same kernel value. Thus all the stated corrected-center, homogeneous-center, and validity-range conclusions follow under their checked hypotheses.

The section-space bijection gives dim W_m=dim V_m. The exact eventual dimension formula and its asymptotics in w7-1/n2 consequently prove
(dim W_m)/m^n→D>0,  log(dim W_m)/log m→n.
The intrinsic exponent is the base section-growth exponent n rather than N=n+f. This conclusion follows from global section descent and production, not from a heuristic about curvature rank.

6. Global measures. For continuous A the exact kernel equality and pushforward give
∫_X A B_X,m dν_X=∫_Y T_A B_m dν_Y.
The base theorem gives m^(−n)B_mν_Y ⇒ ρν_Y, where ρ=(ω^n/n!)/ν_Y is smooth and nonnegative. Since T_A is continuous, the right side after division by m^n tends to ∫_Y T_Aρdν_Y. Fiber integration identifies this last integral with ∫_X A(ρ∘π)dν_X. This proves
m^(−n)B_X,mν_X ⇒ (ρ∘π)ν_X.
Its mass is ∫_Yρdν_Y=D. Alternatively, the L^1 base convergence established in the supporting proof gives the direct stronger estimate
∫_X|B_X,m/m^n−ρ∘π|dν_X=∫_Y|B_m/m^n−ρ|dν_Y→0.
Since dim W_m/m^n→D, the dimension-normalized measures have the indicated probability limit. Finally their unnormalized trace is ∫_XB_X,m dν_X=dim W_m. Thus m^(−N)B_X,mν_X has total mass tending to zero when f>0, and positivity proves its zero weak limit. This verifies every global normalization with the intrinsic exponent.

7. Nonempty compact realizations and limitations. For any connected compact Hermitian F of dimension f≥1, choose a smooth positive ν_F of mass one. The product X=Y×F is compact Hermitian, projection is a holomorphic submersion with connected fibers, E=π*L and its metric are pullbacks, and ν_Yν_F is matched. At p=(x,p_F) the construction in step 2 gives the isolated non-descending selector, so these are genuine examples of all hypotheses.

More generally W(y,u)ν_Yν_F is a smooth positive matched volume whenever ∫_F W(y,u)dν_F(u)=1. Taking nonconstant smooth real b_0 and c with ∫_Fc dν_F=0, and a sufficiently small nonzero δ, gives W=1+δb_0c>0 with this property and a nonproduct volume. Such functions exist on these positive-dimensional compact manifolds. The conformal metric argument in step 1 makes these volumes Hermitian volumes. Steps 1–6 used only submersion charts and compact connected fibers, so the transfer does not otherwise require a product total space.

The exact descent argument relies on connected compact fibers and a pullback bundle. The exact isometry relies on a pullback metric and a matched smooth volume, or on keeping the explicitly transformed base volume. The selector was explicitly computed; a different fiber singularity need not impose the same condition on fiber-constant sections. Hence no result here extends to arbitrary fiber-selected singularities, disconnected fibers, non-pullback bundles or metrics, singular Hilbert norms, or mixed anisotropic base remainders. In particular this sufficient-condition construction makes no claim to solve the unrestricted higher-dimensional programme or the arbitrary-weight one-dimensional problem.
